subject: APAC/EU private deployment — VPC failover and data residency clarifications
messages:

Subject: Private deployment: APAC/EU residency + failover requirements

Jonas —

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. As we discussed with FinBank legal and cloud/security, we're starting to map requirements for a private (VPC/on-prem) deployment of Redwood for production traffic in both EU and APAC. High-level asks:

- Data residency: customer PII and transaction traces must remain at-rest within the originating region (EU or APAC).
- Failover: we need a clear cross-region failover plan that preserves regulatory constraints (cannot automatically copy certain logs outside region).
- KMS/HSM: per-region CMKs required; key material must be region-scoped.
- Telemetry: limit outbound telemetry to only anonymized metrics; raw logs must not leave region without explicit consent.
- Auditability: monthly audit bundles and on-demand audit logs for SOC2/RegX.

I've attached a questionnaire with specifics we filled out for the legal team (FinBank-deploy-questions.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood’s Private option supports a multi-region private topology (two private control planes or single control plane + region agents), and what tradeoffs you see for active-active vs active-passive failover given the residency constraints?

Propose a short architecture review next week — available Tues/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alex Mitchell
Head of Cloud Security — FinBank

Subject: Re: Private deployment: APAC/EU residency + failover requirements

Alex —

Appreciate the detail. Short answer: yes, we can meet the constraints, but the recommended topology depends on two variables: (1) whether you require customer-managed control plane (Private) vs Redwood-managed control plane inside your VPC, and (2) whether you accept cross-region replication for non-sensitive artifacts (models, container images) while keeping PII and logs region-bound.

Two practical architectures we commonly propose:

1) Regional-private, active-passive (lowest regulatory surface):
   - Deploy fully private inference stacks in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 inside your VPCs.
   - Primary handles traffic for its region; passive replica in the other region stays ready (warm) and requires manual or orchestrated failover.
   - No customer PII or raw request logs leave the region. Model artifacts can be replicated as encrypted blobs if you permit cross-region artifact sync.

2) Federated control plane + regional data planes (operationally flexible):
   - A control plane (can be customer-managed) coordinates deployments, rollouts, and metrics metadata.
   - Regional data planes hold runtime state and encrypted request logs; encryption keys are per-region CMKs (HSM/KMS).
   - Smart routing at the edge sends requests to the correct regional data plane; in failover, routing switches while honoring data residency policies (no new copies of restricted logs).

Tradeoffs: active-active provides better latency but complicates residency since writes must be strictly tagged and stored conditionally in-region; active-passive reduces cross-region exposure but increases failover time and testing needs.

Practical asks we need from your infra/security:
- Confirm whether FinBank will require customer-managed control plane (Private) or allow Redwood to host the control plane inside FinBank network.
- List of services/data considered "restricted" vs "non-restricted" (we'll provide tagging rules).
- KMS/HSM access pattern and whether cross-account grants are allowed for automated artifact sync.

I've attached a draft design doc for APAC/EU private topology with diagrams (redwood-apac-eu-private-deploy-draft.pdf) and a short checklist for failover validation. Can we lock a 60m call Wed 15:00 PT? Link: https://calendly.com/redwood/finbank-deploy-review-60m

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Vivek —

A few follow-ups from product/compliance perspective before the call:

- Residency enforcement: we should implement a region-tagging middleware that prevents persisted traces from being written to blob stores outside the region. This would be enforced at the data-plane write layer.
- Telemetry isolation: provide an opt-out flag per-deployment that disables raw request logs from being forwarded to Redwood-managed observability backends. For customers who opt out, we recommend push-based anonymized metrics only.
- KM S pattern: recommend per-region CMKs with automatic key rotation; if FinBank wants cross-region replication of models, we must implement cross-account grants and double-encrypt artifacts so the replica can only be decrypted by the destination KMS.
- Testing: propose quarterly failover drills (staged) + a canary failover run as part of cutover. Ticketed as INFRA-1342 for infra tracking.

I added notes to the draft doc in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3RedwoodDrafts (see the "Residency controls" section).

- Monica

Looping Alex so FinBank sees the proposed technical constraints.

From an infra/networking perspective:

- Network topology: we will use VPC peering / PrivateLink for operator access; no public ingress permitted. Control-plane traffic (if customer-managed) runs on the management VPC peered only with the data-plane VPCs.
- Model artifacts: store as encrypted objects in regional buckets; artifact sync can happen over S3 cross-region replication but only for artifacts flagged as non-sensitive.
- KV cache & runtime state: KV caches and ephemeral token caches must not be replicated; on failover the passive region will rebuild caches on first traffic. Plan for a warm-up window to avoid latency spikes.
- Failover mechanics: route via external DNS with low TTL + health checks; we also support BGP-based failover if you operate an on-prem edge.
- Audit bundles: provide per-region audit bundles (encrypted) delivered to a customer S3 endpoint on schedule.

Operational action items I recommend adding to the MAP:
1) Confirm list of restricted artifacts/files.
2) Provide KMS principal ARNs for cross-account grants.
3) Approve weekly smoke test plan for 2 weeks pre-cutover.
4) Approve timeline for artifact sync window (if any).
